title: Education & EdTech

needs.title: Interest is not reaching the right programme

needs.title: Important information is difficult to find

needs.title: Counselling follow-up is scattered

needs.title: Teams see enquiries but not the journey

definition.title: What is education marketing?
definition.body: Education marketing helps an institution or learning business explain its programmes and reach suitable learners. Useful course pages, accurate information, relevant search visibility and organised counselling work together. The objective is an informed next step, shaped around your admissions calendar, learner needs and available capacity.

services.title: Education website & course pages
services.description: Present programme details, entry requirements, delivery format, fees, schedules and useful FAQs. Build clear enquiry or application routes around the institution's process.

services.title: Education SEO & campus discovery
services.description: Research programme, career-learning and location intent. Improve course content and eligible campus profiles while keeping online-only and physical-location visibility needs distinct.

services.title: Intake and programme campaigns
services.description: Plan suitable advertising around the audience, intake window and course offering. Align ads with accurate landing-page information and the counselling team's ability to respond.

services.title: Content that answers real questions
services.description: Create course explainers, faculty introductions, learning-format previews and approved learner stories. Qualifications, recognition and outcome claims are checked with the institution before use.

services.title: Admissions CRM & counselling follow-up
services.description: Organise enquiry source, programme interest, assigned counsellor and next action. Add agreed acknowledgements and reminders, with staff responsible for admissions advice and decisions.

services.title: Enquiry-to-application visibility
services.description: Review programme interest, suitable enquiries, attended counselling and application milestones where the data is available. Separate campaign activity from verified enrolment outcomes.

process.title: Define the programme and learner
process.description: Confirm the courses, learning formats, locations, audience, entry information and intake calendar. Identify who approves content and owns counselling follow-up.

process.title: Make course information useful
process.description: Review the website, programme pages, enquiry routes and proof that can be substantiated. Resolve unclear eligibility, schedule, fee or recognition information before promotion.

process.title: Reach relevant learners
process.description: Combine suitable search content, social communication and campaigns around the agreed programme and audience. Choose channels because they fit the decision journey, not because every platform must be used.

process.title: Connect enquiries to counselling
process.description: Give each enquiry an owner, programme context and next action. Test any acknowledgement, reminder and handover flow before it supports the admissions team.

process.title: Review the quality of the journey
process.description: Compare sources, relevant enquiries and available counselling or application milestones. Use the team's feedback to improve information, targeting and follow-up over time.

metrics.title: Programme-relevant visibility
metrics.description: Search and campaign activity connected with the courses and learners you intend to reach.

metrics.title: Suitable enquiries
metrics.description: Enquiries that match the agreed programme, location and learning format.

metrics.title: Counselling follow-through
metrics.description: Contact status, attended conversations and outstanding next actions where the team records them.

metrics.title: Application milestones
metrics.description: Applications or enrolments reported from the institution's own reliable records, separately from lead counts.

faqs.question: Do you work with schools, colleges, coaching businesses and EdTech?
faqs.answer: The approach can be adapted to each, but they should not use an identical campaign. Parents, school leavers, working professionals and institutional buyers have different questions and decision journeys. We first review the offering, learner audience, delivery format, geography and admissions process.

faqs.question: Can you help us market a particular course or intake?
faqs.answer: Yes. A focused programme or intake can be a sensible starting point. We review its information, available capacity, audience and counselling process, then agree suitable content and channels. Programme availability, deadlines and claims must remain accurate as the campaign runs.

faqs.question: When should an institution start marketing an intake?
faqs.answer: Planning should begin early enough to prepare clear information, approvals, tracking and enquiry handling before promotion is needed. The right lead time varies with the programme and learner's decision cycle. We work backwards from the admissions calendar instead of promising one fixed campaign period for every institution.

faqs.question: Will AI counsel students or make admissions decisions?
faqs.answer: An assistant may answer approved administrative questions or collect programme interest when included in the scope. Staff remain responsible for individual guidance, eligibility checks and admissions decisions. Conversations involving children or sensitive information require an appropriately designed process and suitable human oversight.

faqs.question: How do you handle placement, selection and recognition claims?
faqs.answer: We use evidence supplied and verified by the institution, with the necessary approvals and context. We do not invent selection rates, guaranteed placements or success stories. Where recognition is relevant, the specific programme and current academic session should be checked rather than relying on a general claim.

faqs.question: Can you use our existing website, CRM or admissions software?
faqs.answer: Yes, we assess what already works and which connections are practical. The proposal sets out content, campaigns, follow-up responsibilities and any integration work. We also agree how performance will be reviewed, using available counselling and application records instead of assuming every enquiry becomes an enrolment.

timing: Plan around the admissions cycle or rolling-cohort schedule. We agree the foundation work, approval responsibilities, campaign launch conditions and review points before promotion. The scope depends on the number of programmes, locations, existing tools and follow-up process; advertising spend and third-party charges are identified separately where relevant.
